newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shares extend loss, seen falling further.
newsitem.headline: Polish shares extend loss, seen falling further.

text.p: Polish shares fell in lower turnover for the seventh consecutive session on Thursday and analysts said the stronger selling after price fixing signalled another loss on Friday.
The main market's WIG index fell 2.7 percent, to 13,745.6, and turnover fell 11.8 percent to 99.3 million zlotys ($35.5 million) on both markets as 71 issues fell, four rose and five were flat.
Analysts said that though the overall macroeconomic situation remained positive the market seemed weak after breaking strong support at 14,000 points and falling to 13,745.6 on Thursday.

"Some stocks should rebound tomorrow but you can't rule out an overall market fall, and it's difficult to say how deep the market will slip before it bottoms out," said Stanislaw Kutkowski, a trader at Wielkopolski Bank Kredytowy brokerage.
Some analysts said foreign investors might be a bit concerned about political uncertainty in Russia, possibly preferring to take profits after the Polish market's 90-percent surge thus far this year.
But they said the Polish economic climate was positive and that increased capital flow to emerging markets could push the WIG up to 16,000 points by year-end.
Some analysts said the lower house of parliament's unexpected cutting of 1997 personal tax levels for the less wealthy was unlikely to affect the market since the highest levels remained unchanged.
But they said the political turmoil that could arise after the decision could cause some investor concern.
